history.summary: Complex of two ruined Shiva temples at Tala village near the Maniyari River, about 29 km from Bilaspur. Attributed to a Sharabhpuriya ruler (legend says built for his daughters-in-law Devrani and Jethani); the smaller red-sandstone Devrani temple is in good preservation (shrine, antechamber, pavilion with lavishly carved doorway) and is of Gupta style, while the Jethani temple is in ruins with its plan traceable from scattered fragments. The site's most famous find is a ~7-ft-tall, ~5-tonne composite Rudra Shiva statue excavated in front of the Devrani temple, with body parts rendered as animal figures and eight human heads; it is kept in a locked structure under ASI care. Discovered by J.D. Beglar (Cunningham's assistant) in 1873; ASI excavated in 1977 (a silver coin of Sharabhpuriya king Prasannamatra was found); declared a protected monument in 1984.

name: Devrani Jethani Temple Complex, Tala
town_description: Tala (Talagram) is a small village in Bilaspur district, Chhattisgarh, about 29 km from Bilaspur, best known for the Devrani-Jethani temple ruins and the unique composite Rudra Shiva statue found here. The village sits in an agrarian belt near the Maniyari River. Most visitors come as day-trippers from Bilaspur to see the archaeological site.
